42 state attorneys general are moving to block Character.AI from auctioning off 21 million private user chat histories in bankruptcy.

As AI tools integrate deeper into technical workflows and personal data, the boundaries surrounding data privacy and autonomous execution are shifting rapidly.

Here are the key technical and industry developments catching my attention today:

⚖️ Data privacy in bankruptcy: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general has stepped in to prevent Character.AI from auctioning off the private chat logs of over 21 million U.S. accounts during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings.

🤖 Open-source AI agents: n8n launched Nod, a free and open-source AI agent configured with its own dedicated computer and web browser, positioning it alongside tools like OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse, and Anthropic Claude Duet.

📐 Mathematics and formal verification: Anthropic work on formal code verification saw progress with the publication of a much shorter version of the GRH Lean verification project.

🌐 Practical system troubleshooting: Developers continue finding utility for LLMs in consumer hardware, utilizing Claude to analyze local network performance and identify specific router configuration adjustments.

As autonomous agents gain direct browser and system access, balancing operational autonomy with data security becomes essential. Meanwhile, the legal treatment of user conversations during corporate asset liquidation will set a major precedent for software platforms moving forward.

Should user chat histories be legally classified as sellable assets during corporate bankruptcy?
